name: prioritizes listing count before total capacity
input: an exact-fill pair and a higher-capacity singleton in one neighborhood

name: matches the source-shaped downtown examples
input: downtown capacities 5, 3, and 1; an unrelated uptown listing
test:
listings = [
    {'id': 1, 'neighborhood': 'downtown', 'capacity': 5},
    {'id': 2, 'neighborhood': 'downtown', 'capacity': 3},
    {'id': 3, 'neighborhood': 'downtown', 'capacity': 1},
    {'id': 4, 'neighborhood': 'uptown', 'capacity': 20},
]
assert select_group_listings(listings, group_size=6, target_neighborhood='downtown') == [1, 3]
assert select_group_listings(listings, 3, 'downtown') == [2]
assert select_group_listings(listings, 10, 'downtown') == []

name: uses capacity and then input position within the minimum-count tier
input: several feasible singleton listings and equal-capacity ties

name: returns no solution when local capacity is insufficient
input: only one undersized listing in the requested neighborhood
test:
listings = [{'id': 'a', 'neighborhood': 'north', 'capacity': 3}]
snapshot = [listing.copy() for listing in listings]
assert select_group_listings(listings, 4, 'north') == []
assert listings == snapshot

name: minimizes capacity among feasible multi-listing subsets
test:
listings = [{'id': name, 'neighborhood': 'north', 'capacity': capacity} for name, capacity in [('eight', 8), ('seven', 7), ('six', 6), ('four', 4)]]
snapshot = [listing.copy() for listing in listings]
assert select_group_listings(listings, 12, 'north') == ['eight', 'four']
assert listings == snapshot
